title: One seat at a time, and the lens a seat takes is the lens it gives back
context: The owner's report (2026-09-23-seat-changes-must-be-robust, Safari on macOS, build 91ba6850): cycling tank > gunship > SOL-82 > tank leaves the view changed with the tank off to the right, and the gunship's fire is not centred on the reticle. Seat switching is the game's central decision (docs/FUNMAP.md), so the whole cycle matrix was measured before anything was changed: a probe (artifacts/qa/seats.mjs, run through scripts/browser-lock.sh) records the view, the lens, the camera pose, which seats are occupied, the pointer-lock state and the projected screen place of the tank and of the gunship's aim point, before and after every transition of TANK>GUNSHIP>TANK, TANK>SOL-82>TANK, TANK>GUNSHIP>SOL-82>TANK, GUNSHIP>SOL-82 directly and seat>MAP>seat.
outcome: ONE MEASURED CAUSE, FIXED. SOL-82's strip button is caught by src/fx/laser-station.js's own capture handler, which calls stopImmediatePropagation, so the views strip's per-button handler never runs and nothing left the seat the player was already in. Pressing SOL-82 from the gunship therefore opened the orbital seat ON TOP of the gunship's: measured pilot=true, gunshipSeat=true, laserSeat=true, params.view stuck at 'bastion', and camera.fov = 52 (SOL-82's ground lens, LASER_GAME.groundFov) in a seat whose reticle and readout still said 2.6x, i.e. 23.08 degrees. The gunship's camera won (updateCameraGoal asks the pilot before the station) so SOL-82's own ground view never appeared, while its beam burned and its scope inset drew over the gunship's frame. Compounding it, every leave restored a hand-written 68 and 'third' (src/td-tab.js leavePilot and the station host's leave) instead of the camera the player actually had. THE CONTRACT: src/domain/seat-view.js, pure and tested in test/seat-view.mjs -- occupancy is exclusive (vacateFor), and the FIRST seat of a chain records the camera to come back to (baseFor/takeSeatView/restoreSeatView) so a seat entered from a seat inherits that base rather than writing the previous seat's lens over it; a cinematic or derived camera is never a place a leave returns to. Wired through the existing paths: the laser station asks host.vacate() before it sits, and leavePilot and the station's leave both go through one restoreSeat that also drops a pointer lock the hull never asked for. src/td-tab.js is net 0 lines (13505, at budget). AFTER: SOL-82 entered from the gunship is byte-for-byte SOL-82 entered from the tank (fov 52, view third, camera position equal to 1e-3) with no pilot seat left under it, and every return to the hull lands at fov 68, view third, with the tank at screen x = 0.00000 and y = -0.41404 exactly, no seat occupied and no pointer lock. NOT REPRODUCED, and said plainly: in headless Chrome at 1440x900, at devicePixelRatio 1 and at 2, the tank's returned screen x is exactly 0 (the third-person rig places the eye, the tank and the look point in one plane containing the camera's up, so the tank is centred by construction), and all three gunship guns' aim point projects through the live camera to exactly the screen centre the reticle is drawn on -- 0.00 px and 0.000 degrees for the rotary, the bofors and the MK-9. The right-shift the owner sees in Safari was therefore not measured; the lens error above is the one mechanism found that changes the gunship's frame without changing its reticle, and it is fixed. Safari could NOT be exercised: 'do JavaScript' from Apple Events is refused (the Develop-menu permission cannot be granted without the operator, and the Safari container's preferences are not writable from here) and the background computer-use daemon is not onboarded, so no screenshot or DOM read of Safari was possible. The fix is Chrome-verified only. Pre-existing and unrelated: --gunship fails at 'the HUD refuses in its own words' (the HUD reads the initial dash because the pass has already ended by the time the tube safes into SPENT) identically on main at 04e61da9 and on this branch.
alternatives: A devicePixelRatio right-shift (the reticle in CSS px over a canvas in device px): disproved by measurement -- the aim projects to the exact screen centre at dpr 1 and dpr 2 alike, and the reticle's SVG viewBox is xMidYMid over a full-window box, so its centre is the element's centre at any ratio.

holdAim's accumulated compensation (src/sentry-pilot.js) applied on the wrong basis or persisting past a leave: ruled out by reading the frame order -- gunshipOptic.ride() runs before pilot.gunshipTick() in the same tick (src/td-tab.js), the impact point and the camera are built from the same eye, direction and up, and headSeen is cleared on dismount. The measured aim offset is zero.
The gunship's aim computed one frame stale against a turning platform: the same frame-order reading rules it out; holdAim holds the WORLD aim, so the reticle and the impact share one direction.

Restoring the tank's camera by leaving the hard-coded 68 and 'third' in place and only fixing the double seat: rejected, because the hard-coded pair is itself the reported 'the view is changed' -- a player who took a seat from the map came back to the chase camera.
Making updateCameraGoal prefer the SOL-82 seat over the pilot when both are live: rejected as treating the symptom; two seats occupied at once is the defect, not the order they are asked in.
evidence: npm test (121 test programs, including the new test/seat-view.mjs) and npm run check green.
scripts/browser-lock.sh node scripts/browser-test.mjs --seats: PASS seats-tank, PASS seats-gunship, with 'rotary/bofors/heavy lands 0.00 px across, 0.00 px down from the reticle at fov 23.0769'.
The --seats step is proven non-vacuous: commenting out the station's host.vacate() call trips 'and the gunship seat is LEFT, not kept underneath it'.
scripts/browser-lock.sh node scripts/browser-test.mjs --laser-game, --defense, --skip-tutorial, --phone: all 'Browser acceptance passed'.
--gunship fails identically at 04e61da9 (main) and on this branch: pre-existing, not this change.
artifacts/qa/seats.mjs (ignored): the before and after cycle matrix at dpr 1 and dpr 2, with the two-seats-at-once row and its 52 vs 23.08 degree lens.
src/domain/seat-view.js, test/seat-view.mjs, src/fx/laser-station.js, src/td-tab.js (seatState acceptance hook, restoreSeat, enterPilot's snapshot).
